name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set contains 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions authored for human standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset also includes the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science-related sentences mined from the Web.
creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2)
citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected from a variety of standardized test sources through several months of extensive search and investigation. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science. Queries were automatically constructed by instantiating approximately 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools. The top several documents from each search were collected, de-duplicated, and stripped down to capture just the text, then chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Document analysis, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 11 question words, mainly proper nouns, do not appear in the ARC Corpus.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from a variety of standardized test sources including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, AMP, CA Standards Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assessment Program, Maryland School Assessment, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous content partner of AI2), MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Standards of Learning, and WASL. The ARC Corpus was sourced from web documents retrieved via a major search engine and augmented with the AristoMini corpus (Wiktionary definitions, Simple Wikipedia science articles, and additional web science sentences).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. The Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based (IR) algorithm and a word co-occurrence (PMI) algorithm. The IR solver uses the Waterloo corpus and Elasticsearch to find sentences supporting each answer option. The PMI solver computes pointwise mutual information between question n-grams and answer option n-grams. Questions answered correctly by either solver were placed in the Easy Set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus: top documents from search queries were collected and de-duplicated, content was stripped to capture just text, and text was chunked into sentences. For the question set: questions were filtered to include only non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions. Questions were partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets based on performance of IR and PMI solvers. For baseline entailment models: questions were converted to Fill-In-The-Blank statements, wh-words replaced with blanks, phrases like 'of the following' dropped, and blanks replaced with answer choices to generate hypotheses. Long sentences (>300 characters), sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered from retrieved premises.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (for IR-based retrieval and filtering), Open IE (for structured representation extraction in DGEM model), AllenNLP (framework for neural baseline models)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM), and a leaderboard are all publicly available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. A leaderboard is maintained for up-to-date results.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive progress in AI research on advanced question answering, moving beyond factoid retrieval-style tasks toward questions requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension. It is designed to encourage research on more difficult AI challenges rather than incremental improvements on simple algorithms.
rai:dataBiases: The Challenge Set is defined operationally as questions answered incorrectly by both IR and PMI solvers, which may bias the set toward questions that are hard for retrieval and co-occurrence methods specifically, rather than all types of hard questions. Approximately 75% of documents in the ARC Corpus were judged as 'science relevant' from an informal analysis, suggesting some non-science content may be present.
rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition only approximates the informal goal of 'hard' questions, as it is defined by failure of two specific baseline solvers. The ARC Corpus, while covering knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of Challenge questions, may not contain all necessary commonsense knowledge. Simple retrieval methods are insufficient to exploit the corpus knowledge for many questions. The question-to-assertion conversion for entailment models can produce non-grammatical sentences in some cases.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for question answering systems. The dataset is intended for use in developing and evaluating AI systems that require advanced reasoning, knowledge, and language understanding beyond simple retrieval. The ARC Corpus is provided as an optional resource for corpus-based approaches; systems are not restricted to this corpus. The dataset includes train/dev/test partitions for both the Challenge and Easy sets.
